solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Book one occupies young children very much

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit within it, so book and one go inside the children

parts.note: tots are small children
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A book that keeps small children thoroughly absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' tempts you toward a title such as TOBIT from the Apocrypha, but here it is just B, which goes with I into TOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bits is an informal British idiom for enormously, as in 'loves her to bits'.

clue.text: Time artist spent working in part of church

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist

indicators.note: something working is in operation, read here as the letters being set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: An artist puts in hours of labour in a section of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts; NSEPT is SPENT rearranged by 'working'.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm crossing the nave in a cross-shaped church building.

clue.text: Resilient, lad reportedly tense following article

indicators.note: following puts the tense after the article in the answer
reportedly means as people say it, so a word sounding like the synonym is wanted

parts.note: a lad is a boy
an is the indefinite article
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tough young man who is said to be on edge after a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article; the homophone gives a floating marker, not a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant describes something that bounces back or stays cheerful, the spirit of being resilient.

clue.text: Hallucinatory experience on Ecstasy? Nonsense!

parts.note: a trip is a drug-induced hallucinatory episode
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses talk of a drug-fuelled vision as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, literally stomach lining eaten as food, is British slang for worthless talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Model intoxicated? Refrain from taking action

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fashion model is drunk, then advising patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit tight is an idiom meaning wait and do nothing for the moment.

clue.text: Running in red vest, toff, one who identifies with the lower classes?

definitions.text: one who identifies with the lower classes?

indicators.note: running suggests letters set in motion and ending up in a new order

parts.note: a nob is a British upper-class person, like a toff

explanation.surface: A posh man jogging in a red vest, as if pretending to be working-class.
explanation.walkthrough: INVERTEDS comes from the letters of IN RED VEST; a toff and a nob are both British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: An inverted snob scorns upper-class taste and champions working-class tastes and manners instead.

clue.text: Restaurant served up excellent crumble and pastry dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: A1, first-rate, is written AI in crosswords
to rot is to decay and crumble
a tart is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A menu offering a fine crumble and a tart for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: AI is A1 with the figure read as a letter; AIROTTART read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian eating house serving informal meals.

clue.text: Formidable champion may make one pull a face

parts.note: grim can mean forbidding or formidable
an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A fearsome sports champion could make a rival wince.
explanation.definitionFit: To grimace is to twist the features in pain or disgust, the same as making an ugly expression.

clue.text: One behind the other inside Accident and Emergency

indicators.note: inside says the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Patients queuing single file in a hospital casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: Accident and Emergency is the British name for a hospital casualty unit; the answer spans accidenT AND EMergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandem describes things arranged in a line, one in front of another, like a two-seat bicycle.

clue.text: Handsome youth, coming from a party, turned evil

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: sin is wickedness, evil

explanation.surface: A young man who left a party and went bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so the name is used for any good-looking young man.

clue.text: Flying through in it on a special

indicators.note: in places the word for through within the rearranged letters
special, as in specially arranged, signals the letters rearranged

parts.note: via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: Flying with a special offer, perhaps on a charter flight.
explanation.walkthrough: IT ON A rearranged by 'special' gives ATION, and VIA goes inside after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviation is the business and activity of flight by aircraft.

clue.text: Result of game if grass allowed to grow wild?

indicators.note: growing wild means running out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football pitch left unmown might stop anyone scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that long grass would stop goals; GRASS ALLOWED has exactly the twelve letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalless draw is a football match ending nil-nil, an outcome of the game.

clue.text: Put on ring (gold) in players' entrance

parts.note: to put on a play is to stage it, so staged
O is ring-shaped
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone wears a gold ring as they come in through the actors' door.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage door is the rear door of a theatre used by actors and staff.

clue.text: Discover the whereabouts of leader of toppled nation

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a race can mean a people or nation

explanation.surface: Hunting down an ousted national leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace someone is to track down and locate them.

clue.text: After parking it by centre, row about stray dog

indicators.note: after puts the following pieces behind the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the bull is the centre of a target, the bullseye

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for row wraps the word for stray

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray

explanation.surface: A dog breaks free from a dispute in the middle of a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of a dartboard or archery target is the bullseye, often shortened to bull.
explanation.definitionFit: The pit bull terrier is a muscular breed of dog originally bred for fighting.

clue.text: Top university job enthralling for each male

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the job holds the other letters

parts.note: a post is a job
per means for each

explanation.surface: A senior university post is enthralling to every man.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means highest or at the very summit, as the word top does as an adjective.

clue.text: Established writer curtails broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: an author is a writer; to dock is to cut short or curtail

explanation.surface: An established writer trims a radio piece.
explanation.walkthrough: AUTHOR DOCKS, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means conventional or traditional, as accepted practice is.

clue.text: Cheeky kid, one stealing fish

parts.note: to whip is British slang for to steal, so a whipper is a thief
a snapper is a fish

explanation.surface: An impudent child who nicks fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is an insolent, presumptuous young person.

clue.text: Journalist noticed hand tool

parts.note: a hack is a journalist
saw means noticed

explanation.surface: A reporter spots a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for metal, worked by hand.

clue.text: The characters one shouldn't forget?

parts.note: characters are letters, two of which feature in the saying about minding one's manners

explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' seems to mean people, but it means letters of the alphabet, from the phrase 'mind your Ps and Qs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Minding your Ps and Qs is an idiom for remembering your manners.

clue.text: Shot of Mike in queue with daughter

indicators.note: in places the letter for Mike within the queue

parts.note: a file is a line or queue
Mike is M in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A photo of Mike standing in line with his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot in the past-tense sense of photographed or recorded on camera.

clue.text: Suffer at home having endless wind

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: endless means losing the last letter of the word

parts.note: to wind something round is to curl it

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at home with constant flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' suggests breeze or gas, but it is the verb, rhyming with 'find': to curl.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to undergo or bring it upon oneself.

clue.text: Small blue train, one lagging behind

parts.note: blue means sad, low
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A little blue toy train that falls behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is British slang for a person who moves or works slowly.

clue.text: The end is nigh

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a conclusion or end

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a doom-monger's cry; split it after 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a noun for a finish and as an adjective for nearness.

clue.text: Fail to see our island state

parts.note: to miss something is to fail to see it

explanation.surface: Overlooking our own island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is a US state in the Midwest, named after its river.

clue.text: Immoral type almost executed

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
to execute a task is to do it, so did

explanation.surface: A wicked character very nearly put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' suggests killing, but it means performed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid means morally vile or squalid.

clue.text: Business centre in Newry, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a city's commercial heart
second meaning: Newry is a town in County Down

explanation.walkthrough: Newry is a town in County Down, Northern Ireland, read as DOWN TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtown is the central commercial district of a city, and also a punning label for a Down settlement.

clue.text: Western county in former kingdom

parts.note: Essex is an English county east of London

explanation.surface: A western county that was once a separate kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex was the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the West Saxons in southern England.
